units.text: The Emancipation Proclamation applied to states and parts of states in rebellion against the United States as of January 1, 1863.

judgement.reason: The passages state that on January 1, 1863, all slaves in any State or designated part of a State whose people were then in rebellion against the United States would be free.

units.text: Louisiana was listed as a state in rebellion under the Emancipation Proclamation.

judgement.reason: The proclamation explicitly orders and designates Louisiana (with stated parish exceptions) as a state in rebellion against the United States.

units.text: The Parishes of St. Bernard, Plaquemines, Jefferson, St. John, St. Charles, and Orleans, including New Orleans, were explicitly exempted from the Emancipation Proclamation.

judgement.reason: The passage explicitly lists St. Bernard, Plaquemines, Jefferson, St. John, and St. Charles as exempted, but it is truncated and does not mention Orleans or New Orleans.

units.text: New Orleans was under Union control on January 1, 1863, and was therefore excluded from the areas where the Emancipation Proclamation took effect.

judgement.reason: The passages explicitly list New Orleans among areas under Union control on January 1, 1863, and state it was exempted from the Emancipation Proclamation.

units.text: The Emancipation Proclamation did not apply to areas already under Union control, including specific parishes in Louisiana such as Orleans Parish.

judgement.reason: The passages state the Proclamation exempted areas under Union control, including New Orleans and 13 named Louisiana parishes, with Orleans explicitly named among them.

units.text: The claim that the Emancipation Proclamation covered New Orleans is contradicted by the explicit exemption of the city and surrounding parishes in the proclamation text and historical records.

judgement.reason: The passages state that New Orleans and 13 nearby parishes were explicitly exempted from the Emancipation Proclamation, which contradicts any claim that it covered New Orleans.
